results.summary: This project implements a 4x4 array multiplier in Verilog that computes the product of two 4-bit binary numbers using partial products and full adders. It is a combinational circuit with 8 input pins for the two operands and 8 output pins for the 8-bit product. Testing is done by applying two 4-bit inputs and verifying the binary product against expected decimal values. The design is a straightforward educational example of structural binary multiplication.

This is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit numbers to produce an 8-bit result using partial products and full adders. It is intended to be tested with a testbench that applies various input combinations and compares the output to expected binary multiplication results. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. It is a typical educational project demonstrating structural multiplication.

This design implements a digital low-pass and decimation filter intended for the output of a delta-sigma analog-to-digital converter. It accepts a 1-bit input at 50 MHz and produces 16-bit filtered data on the GPIOs at a decimated rate of 781.25 kHz. The project includes clock division outputs and is planned to be paired with an analog frontend on a future shuttle. Testing involves feeding a 1-bit delta-sigma modulated signal and observing the decimated output.

This project is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit inputs to produce an 8-bit product using full adders. The documentation suggests testing with negative numbers in two's complement form, though the design is described as a standard unsigned multiplier. It is a combinational circuit with no external hardware requirements. The project appears to be a student lab exercise.

This is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using partial products and full adders to produce an 8-bit result. The documentation includes a generic hardware testing procedure that is not specific to the multiplier, suggesting limited verification detail. The design is combinational and requires no external hardware. It is a student lab project.

This project implements a 4x4 structural array multiplier in Verilog that multiplies two 4-bit binaries using full adders. It includes a Python testbench (test.py) where users can set input values and expected outputs to verify functionality. The design is combinational and requires no external hardware. It is an educational project from a course (ECE2204).

This is a 4x4 array multiplier that generates partial products via AND gates and sums them with full adders to produce an 8-bit product. Testing is suggested through simulation with a testbench covering multiple cases including minimum and maximum values to check carry propagation. The design is combinational and requires no external hardware. It is a typical educational implementation.

This project is a 4x4 array multiplier that takes two 4-bit inputs, m and q, and produces an 8-bit product p using partial products and full adders. Testing involves parsing an 8-bit value into two 4-bit operands and verifying the product. The design is combinational and requires no external hardware. It is a student lab project.

This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that generates four partial products by ANDing bits of two 4-bit inputs and sums them with binary adders to yield an 8-bit product. Testing can be done by applying all 256 possible input combinations or key cases to verify the output. The design is combinational and requires no external hardware. It is an educational project.

This is a 2-bit flash analog-to-digital converter that converts an analog input voltage between 0 and 1.8 V into a 2-bit encoded digital output. It uses analog pins for the input and digital outputs for the encoded result. Testing is done by applying a voltage to the analog pin and observing the two output bits. The design is implemented in analog and is a simple example of a flash ADC.
